title: Four Muslim nations sign the 'Badr' defence pact
credits: Photos: Popup Agency, Eko Herwantoro, Cengiz Özarpat, Sushanta Rokka / Unsplash · Map: Natural Earth
lines: Four Muslim countries have just signed a new defence deal, and they have named it Badr.
Pakistan, Türkiye, Qatar and Indonesia signed the memorandum in Doha, on Wednesday the twenty-first of October.
Pakistan's defence minister, Khawaja Asif, signed for Islamabad.
Türkiye's defence minister, Yaşar Güler, and Qatar's deputy prime minister, Sheikh Saoud bin Abdulrahman, also signed.
Indonesia was represented by its deputy defence minister, Yusuf Jauhari.
According to Türkiye's defence ministry, the pact covers defence production, military exercises and training, and research and development.
Middle East Eye reports that joint production facilities are expected to be set up in Türkiye, with Qatar contributing funding and technology.
The name refers to the Battle of Badr, in the year six hundred and twenty-four. Türkiye's ministry says Badr also means full moon.
Gulf states are keen on cheaper air defence, after the Iran war strained their systems, and American alternatives face long delivery queues.
Together, these four countries are home to more than six hundred million people.
Pakistan's Foreign Office had not commented on the deal at the time of reporting.
